spec_match.rationale: The shared shim in zip.js was written from the proposal's numbered steps after reading the spec text, not from recollection — which corrected a claim this build had already written into a page, that padding with a non-longest mode is a TypeError. It is not: padding is read only under longest and is otherwise not validated, so it fails silently. The page now says that, and says why it is worth knowing.

interactive.rationale: Three live surfaces: editable ragged sources running all three modes at once with a step-by-step table for the focused one, a column-to-record transposer over pasted data, and three instrumented generators walked with a chosen exit path.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index frames the feature as making two decisions explicit — what happens when lengths differ, and who gets closed — which is the proposal's own motivation, and each card matches what its page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Ragged and equal-length inputs, all three modes, padding shorter than the source count, strict throwing mid-walk after yielding usable rows, empty columns, and three distinct walk endings (early break, exhaustion, consumer throw).

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/6249068542164992 on the index and all three concept pages, with the TC39 repository and the rendered specification text.

conformance.rationale: Eight immutable assertions covering both statics, the shortest default, the unknown-mode TypeError, longest padding substitution, the strict throw landing at the diverging step after two values have already been yielded, and the IteratorCloseAll guarantee proved with a generator finally block.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150, twice: with V8 staging off (3/3, 21 assertions, shim path) and with --js-flags=--harmony on (3/3, 21 assertions, native Iterator.zip/zipKeyed). Both paths close every abandoned generator on all three exit routes, verified by reading flags the generators set themselves. The native path pulls one value fewer at the final step than the shim, which the page reports as a measured number rather than a fixed claim.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with measured step counts, fill counts, pull counts and whether every source was closed.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour together, 44px control minimums, wide tables in their own overflow-x container.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled inputs and selects, semantic tables with scope and captions that update, the strict-mode failure announced through role=status, and aria-live output summarising each recomputation.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Source, control, mode and sensor grids are all auto-fit minmax with align-content:start so they stack cleanly at 360px; the record table scrolls inside .scroller rather than widening the page.

openQuestions.title: Swap the shim for the native statics once Chrome ships them
openQuestions.detail: Every page already prefers Iterator.zip/zipKeyed when present and says which it is running, so no code change is needed. What will need re-reading is the merge-and-close page: its closing evidence currently proves the shim closes abandoned generators, and once the native path is taken it becomes evidence about the engine — which is the more interesting claim, and the copy should say so directly rather than leaving the reader to infer it.

openQuestions.title: Cover the async form if the proposal grows one
openQuestions.detail: Joint Iteration is currently synchronous only. Several of the motivating use cases — merging two paginated network feeds, walking a reader alongside a timer — are asynchronous, and a reader arriving from those problems will look for AsyncIterator.zip. Nothing to build until the proposal has it, but worth watching.

guidanceConsulted.query: live region for results updated by a button
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce recomputed results and error states through live regions rather than colour or position alone, and keep every control labelled.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each page writes a narrative summary into an aria-live output on every recompute; the strict-mode TypeError renders into a role=status element so it is announced rather than only tinted, and padded cells are marked by text as well as colour.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive asserts the detail text and the error text on each run.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Auto-fit grids for panels of controls; give wide tabular content its own scroll container.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All four grids use repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)) with align-content:start; the record table is wrapped in an overflow-x:auto scroller because its column count is driven by user input and cannot be bounded.

summary: Three concepts: the modes seen side by side on the same ragged input, a practical column-to-record transposer, and the cleanup guarantee demonstrated by instrumenting the generators rather than describing it. Reading the spec text before writing the shim corrected a factual error already committed to a page.
